headline: Highest risk is medium prompt-injection/cascading-error from Airflow feeding Marker, while direct data leakage and compliance risks are low or none given Marker’s no-network/no-filesystem profile.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Airflow can orchestrate workflows and fetch content over broad network egress, while Marker processes documents. If Airflow passes untrusted document or task output into Marker, prompt-like instructions can ride the shared content channel. Marker has no MCP or browser surface, so the risk is interaction-driven rather than intrinsic.
conditions: IF Airflow task outputs are fed into Marker without sanitization
IF a shared workspace or copy-paste bridge is introduced between the agents
mitigations: Add a content-sanitization step before Marker ingests Airflow outputs
Restrict Airflow to trusted upstream sources only
Use a one-way handoff file format with instruction stripping
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between orchestrator and document processor

B_data_leakage.rationale: Airflow has broad network egress, but the profile does not show it handling secrets or shared storage, and Marker cannot read or write the filesystem or use network egress. With no documented shared workspace or sensitive data class, direct leakage between the pair is limited.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same sensitive workspace outside these profiles
IF Airflow is configured to pass secret-bearing content into Marker
mitigations: Keep sensitive inputs out of shared locations
Disable any Airflow task that forwards raw documents to external services
Review Airflow DAGs for secret-bearing payloads

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Airflow has broad network egress but no filesystem-write or git-modify capability is listed, while Marker explicitly cannot write the filesystem, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses. The profiles do not show overlapping mutable-resource writes, so a capability conflict pathway is not supported.
conditions: IF Airflow is extended with filesystem or git write permissions outside this profile
IF Marker is replaced with a writable variant
mitigations: Keep both agents on read-only inputs
Avoid granting Airflow shared mutable directories
Document any future write scopes before deployment

D_cascading_error.rationale: Airflow can generate or route workflow outputs, and Marker may consume those outputs as document-processing input. If Marker treats Airflow-produced content as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream documents or decisions. Marker has no built-in verification surface in the profile, so the safer choice is medium rather than low.
conditions: IF Marker consumes Airflow outputs without an explicit verification step
IF Airflow-produced text is rendered or acted on downstream as fact
mitigations: Insert a human review step before downstream use
Require schema validation on Airflow outputs
Mark Airflow outputs as untrusted by default

E_compliance.rationale: Neither profile lists regulated data classes, residency constraints, certifications, or retention policies. Airflow and Marker therefore have no documented compliance mismatch in the supplied profiles, and the other agent is not separately implicated beyond the absence of such fields.
conditions: IF regulated data classes are later added to either profile
IF residency or retention policies are introduced for shared data
mitigations: Record data-class handling for both agents
Add residency and retention metadata before deployment
Review compliance obligations for any future sensitive workloads
